thread:
emily: quick summary from today's bring-up of the compact-v3 variants. ran a 25k mixed holdout with an explicit short/long split + cohesion checks.
hassan: nice. what exact probes did you run?
emily: recall@1/5, mean reciprocal rank, median cosine shift vs float32, cluster cohesion (silhouette k=150), and a neighbor-consistency probe (count neighbors that change rank within top10). also tracked embedding norms and ran a simple KS test between distributions.
jules: please paste the command so I can repro locally.
emily: sure:
```
python eval/onboard_mixed.py \
  --model compact-v3 \
  --variants int8-perchannel,int6-pertensor,float32 \
  --holdout 25000 \
  --short_thresh 7 \
  --long_thresh 60 \
  --k 5 \
  --seed 7
```

emily: top-line numbers (mixed holdout):
- float32: r@1=0.83, r@5=0.95, mrr=0.88, cos_shift=0.00, silhouette_k150=0.44, neigh_change_top10=0.049, norm_ks_p=0.45
- int8-perchannel: r@1=0.81, r@5=0.94, mrr=0.86, cos_shift=0.018, silhouette_k150=0.42, neigh_change_top10=0.058, norm_ks_p=0.11
- int6-pertensor: r@1=0.73, r@5=0.89, mrr=0.78, cos_shift=0.09, silhouette_k150=0.35, neigh_change_top10=0.19, norm_ks_p=0.002

maria: int8-pc looks close enough overall. int6 is problematic for short queries as usual. any language breakdowns?
emily: did en/es/pt stratification. int8-pc r@1 by lang: en=0.82, es=0.79, pt=0.78. int6: en=0.74, es=0.66, pt=0.65.
hassan: interesting. what about short vs long split?
emily: short (<7 tokens): float32 r@1=0.85, int8-pc=0.83, int6=0.70. long (>60 tokens): float32 r@1=0.80, int8-pc=0.79, int6=0.76. so int6 hits short queries hardest.
jules: did you look at norm histograms? any collapse?
emily: yes. float32 mean norm=11.8 sd=2.4, int8-pc mean=11.0 sd=2.1, int6 mean=6.0 sd=1.3.KS pval int6 vs float32 = 0.002 (significant).
bot-eval: job compact-v3-int8pc-5088888888 started on runner-ml-03 (est 16m)

emily: I also ran a tiny calibration for int6 (2k short queries) with asymmetric centering and re-run: int6-calib r@1 went to 0.76, neigh_change_top10=0.12, cos_shift=0.06. improvement but still below int8-pc.
maria: proposal: default to int8-perchannel for compact-v3 in the model catalog, keep int6 as opt-in with a visible warning and require an onboarding short-tail probe and a mandatory calibration step if chosen.
hassan: agree. also add neighbor-change_top10 threshold <=0.10 and norm_ks_p > 0.01 for acceptance for short-tail sensitive apps.
jules: add the eval args and seed into the catalog metadata; plus attach the 50-example manual inspect sample (top1 neighbors for 50 short queries). that helps product/pm eyeball semantic regressions.
emily: will open PR with changes: default quant profile, onboarding gate updates (short-tail probe + neighbor-change + norm KS), and an opt-in flag for int6 that wires the calibration step automatically.
bot-eval: job compact-v3-int8pc-5088888888 finished (duration 15m)
maria: one more item: collect latency/cost delta for int8 vs int6 in the onboarding report (we need to show the cost win to justify int6 opt-in).
emily: added. int6 size ~38MB, int8-pc ~54MB, median latency int6=5.9ms, int8-pc=7.2ms (on our stack). cost delta about +20% for int8-pc.
hassan: great. proceed with PR and we'll monitor the next week's rollout metrics in the model catalog dashboard.
emily: thanks all, creating ticket now and will attach eval logs + sample csv.
